lawyer:
M. H. Khandker with M.B. Rahman ------- For the Petitioner. 
Mostafa Kamal, Advocate-General with Quazi Shafiuddin Ahmed and A.H. Md. Saadat Ali Khan ------- For the Respondents.
parties:
M/s. Free School Street Property Ltd. Dacca  ------- Petitioner. 
Vs.
Bangladesh and another.  ------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
The petitioner's case in short, is that the petitioner is a company incorporated under the Companies Act with the registered office at Chittagong in Bangladesh and has been owing and possessing the land and buildings in holding No. 118, Segun Bagicha, P.S. Ramna, Dacca, after purchase of the same by the registered deed of conveyance dated 14th July, 1952 for a consideration of Rs. 77,393/9/- annas. The land measuring 19 kattas 4 chattaks belonging to the Government Khas Mohal appertaining to Khas Mohal Estate No. 157 of the Dacca Collectorate was taken in lease for construction of residential buildings by one Rashik Chandra Basu under registered deed dated 9-3-1932 for 29 years from 1st April, 1932 to 31st March, 1961 with right to successive renewal of settlement for further period of years and all rights of transfer, assignment, etc.; and that the lessee constructed buildings on the said land and when he had been ownership and possession thereof, died leaving 5 sons, who sold the land along with buildings for a consideration of Rs. 60,000/- to the Muslim Commercial Bank Ltd. by a registered deed of conveyance dated 6th April, 1948, and that the said Bank conveyed the said property to the petitioner. Since then the petitioner had been in ownership thereof after mutating its name with the lesser landlord and paying rent for the lease-hold interest in the land and municipal and other taxes levied on the holding. Mutation was made in Mutation Case No. 32/53-54 and Khatian No. 13 was prepared in the name of the petitioner. The two storeyed building consists of 4 flats which had been let out by the petitioner to monthly tenants. The premises in question was requisitioned by an order dated 15-1-1972 made in Requisition Case No. 2168/1972 and the tenants were asked to give possession with effect from 17th February, 1972. But on the representation of the petitioner the building was de-requisitioned by the order dated 1st February, 1972 and 8th April, 1972 and possession of the building was restored to the petitioner through the tenants. Subsequently the holding in question was purported to be taken over as abandoned property under Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972 and notice thereof was served upon the petitioner's tenant. 

 2. The petitioner submitted representation in writing to the Government stating that the property in question could not be treated as abandoned property. In the meantime the petitioner submitted an application for renewal of the lease with effect from 1st April, 1961 but no action was taken thereon as per terms of the lease; rather subsequently attempts were made for treating the property as abandoned property. Thereafter the petitioner received a notice from respondent No. 2 to show cause why the lease hold property should not be resumed as the term of 29 years of the lease had expired with the end of 31st March, 1961 and on the ground of violation of the terms of the lease. Thereupon the, petitioner submitted an objection to the said notice on 1st September, 1973 and again prayed for renewal of the lease with effect from 1st April 1961. Thereafter it transpired that the Addl. Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dacca informed the Govt. authority regarding the Abandoned Property matters that the property in question was not an abandoned property but Government khas property; and that the land under lease had been resumed as per terms of the lease and that the land along with building became khasmohal property; and that the petitioner's tenants were asked to vacate possession of the building and to make over possession of the same to the S. A. Kanongo on 25-9-1973 at 2 P.M. failing which action will be taken as per law without any further notice. Thereupon the petitioner submitted a petition to the Govt. praying for relief against the said order or of resumption as per the impugned notice and also prayed for renewal of the lease. This petition was heard by the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh who by his order dated 16th April, 1974 passed in Case No. VI-125/- 73-T rejected the same. Thereafter the petitioner moved this Court on 29th April, 1974 when this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned order should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to cancel, rescind or withdraw the impugned order etc. 

 3. The respondent No. 2, namely, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) has entered appearance and shown cause by filing affidavit-in-opposition. In the affidavit-in-opposition it has been stated, inter alia, that on the death of original lessee Rashik Chandra Basu, his heirs of successors did neither register their names in the Collector rate within three calendar months nor did anything and that on account of violation of the said terms and conditions of the said lease deed and further more the application filed after lapse of about 12 years for renewal could not be considered and the land was resumed as per terms of the lease and land along with building thereon forfeited to the Government; and that the order of resumption on cancellation of the lease having been made in accordance with law, relief as prayed for by the petitioner cannot be granted. 

 5. On consideration of the materials we are satisfied that the petitioner duly acquired the lease hold interest along with building by the registered deed of conveyance dated 14th July, 1952; and that on the expiry of the lease period i.e. 31st March, 1961 an application for renewal of the lease was duly filed, but instead of granting renewal of the lease, as a matter of course, as provided in the lease deed, the authority unnecessarily kept the matter pending for an indefinite period; and that in 1972 the petitioner filed a fresh application for renewal of the lease, but the same was rejected wrongly on 16th April, 1974 by the Secretary of the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The petitioner's claim for renewal is based upon clause 13 of the original lease deed dated 9th March, 1932 which provides that if the lease carries out all the terms of this agreement then on the expiry of the lease he shall be entitled to successive renewals of settlement for farther period of years under such terms as may be offered to him and on payment Of such rent (being a fair rent) as may be assessed. It appears that in view of compliance of the requirement of mutation and acceptance of rent upto 1963, there could not be any valid ground for refusal to renew the lease as prayed for by the petitioner. In that view of the matter, we hold that the order of resumption is illegal and without any lawful authority. We further hold that the order of forfeiture of the building thereon to the Government and refusal to renew the lease in favor of the petitioner is also illegal and without any lawful authority. Therefore, the Rule is made absolute. The petitioner is entitled to costs of this application which is assessed at 35 G. Ms.
